assignments.rationale: Both wrote sustained, candid self-examination: Montaigne's essays on himself, Aurelius's private notebook.
Writings on attention, stillness, and the unity of experience.
Orators whose published speeches and writings show precise, plain, persuasive language.
Method and argument: Franklin's practical reasoning, Maimonides' systematic analysis, Wollstonecraft's sustained case from reason.
Autobiographies that reconstruct memory carefully and draw on it.
Seneca's letters on anger and grief; Churchill's speeches and histories on composure and resolve under strain (owner replaced Osler, 2026-11-06).
Addams on understanding neighbors unlike oneself; Montaigne on the variety of human minds.
Conduct, duty, what is in one's power, and equal moral standing.
Compression of particulars into general principles.
Care grounded in close attention to the people served.
Curie's account of patient experimental work; Franklin's self-tracking and revision of habits.
Teachers, institution builders and statesmen concerned with passing knowledge and duty on (owner replaced Osler with Churchill, 2026-11-06).
Stoic practice of watching one's own judgments before acting on them.
